frontier.hypothesis: A forensic cc1 -da dump of the FLOOR-18 form itself will explain the v0/v1 swap of the selected value in terms of allocno order and conflicts, instead of leaving it to spelling roulette.
frontier.mechanism: s2's only RTL dumps (tmp/grind/func_80034F88/s2/rtl/v10/) are of a pre-lever variant that no longer resembles the current body. The `.greg` dump's `;; Register dispositions` and conflict lists would say WHY the pseudo holding `val2` lands in v1 where target has v0 — target's v0 is the very register `lw v0,0x20(a1)` just used for the condition, so the suspicion is that our condition temporary `c` holds v0 across the block.
frontier.next_probe: Run tmp/grind/func_80034F88/s2/dump_rtl.sh against the current src/ body; read the dispositions and conflict list for the pseudo holding `val2`; then diff against the same dump for a variant with `c` eliminated (`if (!(p[8] & K))` inline) to test whether `c`'s live range is what occupies v0. This is a forensics-modality probe and it is the cheapest remaining honest measurement on the function.
